summary.headline: Orders and revenue both missed target this week, and the year remains behind pace, with the recent revenue run-rate below what's needed to hit the full-year target.

points.what: Orders were 88.4% of target and revenue was 89.6% of target this week, both down week on week.
points.so_what: Both KPIs missed target this week, keeping the quarter behind its target pace.

points.what: Orders grew 73.6% year on year and revenue grew 82.4% year on year, versus the 75% growth built into targets.
points.so_what: Orders growing slightly below the target's growth assumption while revenue grew above it explains why revenue attainment came in higher than orders attainment this week.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue attainment is 94.6% of target.
points.so_what: The recent revenue run-rate remains below what's required for the rest of the year, putting the full-year target at risk.

points.what: The week's order decline was led by North America, down 24.1% week on week, and by Search, down 4.3% week on week.
points.so_what: APAC, EMEA and LATAM orders all grew week on week, so the shortfall was concentrated in one region and one channel rather than broad-based.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of 13 Apr rose to 11.4%, up 0.4pp week on week and up 1.0pp year on year, the second straight weekly increase.
points.so_what: A second consecutive rise means the return-rate trend has not reversed.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue attainment is 98.4% of target, with $561,526 still needed over the remaining 8 weeks of the quarter.
points.so_what: The quarter remains behind target and needs a pickup from the recent pace to close the gap.

points.what: The current 8-week revenue run-rate is $62,467, below the $81,319 weekly run-rate required for the rest of the year.
points.so_what: Holding at the current pace would leave the full-year revenue target out of reach.

points.what: Orders were 88.4% of target and revenue was 89.6% of target this week.
points.so_what: Both landed behind target this week, keeping the quarter behind pace.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue attainment is 98.4% of target, with $561,526 still needed over the remaining 8 weeks of the quarter.
points.so_what: The quarter is close to target but still behind, and needs the remaining weeks to close the gap.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue attainment is 94.6% of target; the required weekly run-rate for the rest of the year is $81,319 versus a current 8-week run-rate of $62,467.
points.so_what: The recent pace is well below what's needed, putting the full-year target at risk.

points.what: North America orders fell 24.1% week on week, contributing -57 orders to the week's decline.
points.so_what: North America's decline outweighed the total order drop, meaning growth in other regions partly offset it.

points.what: Search orders fell 4.3% week on week, contributing -27 orders, which matched the week's entire net order decline.
points.so_what: The week's overall order decline came entirely from Search, since other channels such as Facebook grew instead.

points.what: Facebook orders rose 46.2% week on week, contributing +18 orders.
points.so_what: This growth partly offset the declines from North America and Search but was not enough to prevent an overall drop in orders.

points.what: AOV was $89.18, up 0.3% week on week and up 4.0% year on year.
points.so_what: AOV rose while orders fell week on week, so revenue held up better than order volume did this week.

points.what: The cancellation rate was 14.5%, down 0.8pp week on week and down 0.9pp year on year.
points.so_what: A falling cancellation rate protects revenue, since each percentage point of cancellations is worth about $787.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of 13 Apr was 11.4%, up 0.4pp week on week and up 1.0pp year on year.
points.so_what: Both comparisons point the same direction, marking a second straight weekly rise in returns to watch.

points.what: New signups were 238, flat week on week, and up 8.7% year on year, while orders grew 73.6% year on year.
points.so_what: Signup growth continues to run far behind order growth on a year-on-year basis, widening the gap between new customer acquisition and order volume.
